text:
jamie: Heads-up — started seeing a steady backlog of Pending GPU pods in us-west-2 since ~06:20 UTC. Lots of 1-GPU jobs unable to schedule even though there are free GPU fractions across nodes.

rav: Same. Autoscaler is launching new 4xV100 nodes but they don't help because most queued jobs request 1 GPU each. Binpacking is terrible atm.

sophia: Can you paste a kubectl get pods -o wide for the pending ones? Are they requesting fractional GPUs or whole device plugins?

jamie: They're whole-device requests, e.g. resources: requests: nvidia.com/gpu: "1". Example pod: 
```
Name: training-job-92
Status: Pending
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 6 node(s) had insufficient gpu, 6 node(s) had too many pods.
```

lee: The "too many pods" is interesting — we hit maxPods kubelet limit on some older flavors. Those nodes have free GPUs but no pod capacity.

rav: That plus heterogenous node sizes is causing fragmentation. Autoscaler picks cheapest instance type with 4 GPUs to satisfy big memory workloads; small 1-GPU jobs can't share due to our anti-affinity rules.

jamie: Right. We added podAntiAffinity last quarter to avoid noisy-neighbor interference for large trains. But it's now blocking small batch jobs.

k8s-autoscaler: cluster-autoscaler: scalewindow triggered: scale-up from 6->9 nodes (reason: unschedulable pods). Instance types: p3.x8 -> p3.8xlarge configured.

rav: Quick idea: allow binpack fairness via a "small-pod" nodepool with 1-GPU instances (g4dn.xlarge) and explicit nodeSelector for low-priority / ephemeral jobs. That should reduce fragmentation.

lee: Agree. But cost alert: g4 nodes cost more/hour per GPU because of smaller amortization. We need to balance cost vs schedule latency.

sophia: Could also tweak kube-scheduler scoring plugin to prefer nodes with free GPU devices for small pods. A custom FitScore that weights device fragmentation less aggressively.

jamie: Do we have bandwidth to touch scheduler? Might take longer. Short-term: create a burst nodepool with smaller instances + taint + toleration for job queue. Then let workflows target it via toleration.

rav: How about re-evaluating affinity rules: only apply podAntiAffinity for pods with label scale=large. That way small jobs bypass.

lee: I can spin a test nodepool (us-west-2a) with 8 g4dn.xlarge (1 GPU each) and taint gpu-small=true:NoSchedule. Job queue can get updated via CI to add tolerations. Cost calc: rough estimate $0.9/hr per node * 8 nodes = $7.2/hr. If it removes median wait time (currently 12m) should be worth it for the next 48hrs.

jamie: Please do a single AZ first to reduce cross-AZ placement issues. Also watch pod startup times — we saw previous network attachment timeouts when kubelet pulled drivers concurrently. Add maxParallelPodStarts=10 on the pool.

ops-bot: deploy started: creating nodepool gpu-small-usw2a (count=8, instance=g4dn.xlarge). ETA 4m.

rav: Optional: change cluster-autoscaler config to prefer scaling the new nodepool for pods with label gpu.workload=ephemeral. There is a webhook we can add to annotate pods.

jamie: Good. Sophia, if we still see fragmentation after this, we should consider enabling gpu device plugin MIG/GPU-Sharing prototype for small inference jobs. Not for training.

sophia: A note: enabling MIG requires re-creating nodes with MIG-enabled AMI; not trivial. Let's use nodepool first.

lee: Nodepool is up (ops-bot). I updated 3 non-critical cronjobs to add toleration and they scheduled instantly.

jamie: Nice. Can someone monitor pending queue length and scheduler logs for next 2 hours? I'll open a dashboard for tokenized latency and preemption events.

rav: Monitoring: pending GPU pods dropped from 72 -> 9 in 12 minutes. Avg wait down to 3m.

jamie: Perfect. We'll keep the nodepool for 48h, then analyze cost vs latency and decide whether to keep or convert into an autoscaling pool with min=2,max=20.

lee: I'll also propose a scheduler policy change: only label / enforce anti-affinity for pods with label affinity.scope=exclusive. That gives more control to teams.

sophia: Added to the infra board backlog.

jamie: Thanks all. Action items: 1) lee validate cost after 24h, 2) rav update CA config to prefer gpu-small (if we go autoscale), 3) sophia add scheduler policy RFC.

ops-bot: reminder: nodepool gpu-small-usw2a will be auto-terminated if unused for 72h (policy infra/ephemeral-pools).
